newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan money rates end up on new reserve period.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan money rates end up on new reserve period.

text.p: Taiwan's money rates ended higher on Monday, with banks no longer needing to liquidate excess funds at the start of a new reserve period, dealers said.

The overnight interbank rate was at 5.981 percent against Saturday's 5.445 close -- far outside the central bank's 5.00-5.5 percent target zone -- with 30-day commercial paper rising to 6.00-6.05 percent from 6.00.
Money rates were expected to continue an upswing on Tuesday on relatively tightened fund flow, dealers said.
In the bond market, the 10-year 86/4 bond yield was at 6.0860-0900 against 6.1040.
